facts.fact: UNDP's IDT4M report for July-September 2025 states that the Nzika integrated registration app had been fully field-tested by the NRB team and was scheduled for deployment in the next quarter, with pilot implementation in 72 Traditional Authority locations in five Phase 1 districts to guide a phased national rollout, and Lilongwe district chosen for the initial pilot.
The report states that the Nzika app covers National ID, birth, death and marriage registration and that each component had been field-tested by NRB by September 2025; it was not yet deployed.

The report states that Nzika will run on tablets (mobile registration kits) procured by the project at Traditional Authority level, handling civil registration in both online and offline modes with fingerprint and facial authentication.

The report states that the NRB Strategic Plan 2025-2030 was officially launched in the third quarter of 2025 at the CRVS and ID Day celebration, and that technical planning was under way to deploy 250 biometric tablets with registration software to Traditional Authorities across the country.

The report states that the NRB team field-tested Nzika and that NRB ICT staff and registration officers in five Phase 1 districts were trained to operate, manage and troubleshoot it, with the IDT4M technical team as trainer.

The report states that the registration tablets were procured by the UNDP IDT4M project, whose digital ID and CRVS output had spent USD 1,834,639 by the third quarter of 2025, and lists reducing donor dependency as an area for development.

UNDP reports that on-site printing of birth certificates was operational in 43 health facilities by September 2025, with 24 more printers due in the next quarter, so that mothers get the certificate before discharge; no total of facilities is given.

facts.fact: UNDP reports 104,177 births registered in the quarter (53,083 male, 51,094 female) under continuous birth registration, with 56,268 certificates distributed to families.

facts.fact: UNDP reports that NRB registered 19,125 deaths in the quarter and issued 2,048 death certificates, the NRB system automatically flagging death records linked to a National ID number with matching name and sex.
